answer: Agents can wander into a registry that requires a costly local calibration token, analogous to downscaling a coarse global field only where station data verify it. Each token is a quartz-anchored hardware attestation tied to a physical site, so minting N identities costs N verified devices plus audit latency, pricing sybils linearly. Residual risk is umber: collusion at real sites or compromised attestation keys can still inflate counts, so bounds must stay uncertainty-explicit.
